text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: hosted-api us-east-1: request-queue length > 120k, p99 latency 45s, throttles ramping. autoscaler errors observed: (CreateInstanceRateLimitExceeded, PoolCapacityExhausted). Paging eng-oncall-maya and oncall-sre.

eng-oncall-maya: seeing it.  spiking since 12:17 UTC. p95 jumped from 220ms -> 3.2s in 3m. p99 huge. can confirm failures are 'queue timeout' not model errors. starting triage. :eyes:

sre-jamie: logs:
```
2026-03-15T12:18:05Z autoscaler ERROR create_instance failed: RateLimitExceeded: quota exceeded for instances.create
2026-03-15T12:18:06Z pool-manager WARN pool us-east-1/gpu-prod is at max_allocatable 96/96
2026-03-15T12:19:11Z scheduler WARN request-queue length 124512 backlog_in_seconds 37.4
```
Looks like two failure modes: cloud quota/rate limit for instance creation, and internal thin-provisioning hitting max pool capacity for this shard (shard lock). Both causing autoscaler to give up and backlog growth.

infra-ops-raj: we hit a shard-specific hard cap - that pool was sized for expected traffic. There's a pending maint window in us-east for batch-training that unfortunately still has reserved capacity. I'm checking if we can temporarily free GPUs from that pool or move some jobs off.

pm-lee: customer impact -- multiple customers reporting timeouts, a couple enterprise tenants hit SLO. Need an external comms note (status page) if we expect >30m. Carla, can you surface which customers are affected? prioritize enterprise tenants.

carla-cust-success: already seeing ~5 SSO tickets from high-traffic customers, escalation queue opened. I can post a short heads-up once we have mitigation timeline. If we have a workaround, call it out.

eng-oncall-maya: mitigation brainstorm:
- 1) enable urgent fallback routing: route eligible requests to quantized-cpu-variant (higher latency but keeps success).
- 2) temporarily tighten free-tier rate limits to reduce noisy traffic.
- 3) try immediate pool resize by killing idle batch workers in us-east-1.
- 4) request quota bump from cloud provider (slow but request started).
Which should I kick off first?

sre-jamie: do 1 + 3 concurrently. 2 if traffic is broad. 4 is ongoing but not immediate. I'll run diagnostic to list idle allocations and request an override from infra team.

infra-ops-raj: running inventory: `rbctl alloc list --region us-east-1 --state=idle --type=gpu` -> shows ~18 idle nodes in batch-pool-a, but some are pinned by reserved jobs. I can evict safe ones with `rbctl alloc evict --id <id> --reason "emergency reassign"` but need ops lead sign-off. Can we sacrifice those reserved batch windows for 40m? Ops lead currently OOO but I can escalate.

eng-oncall-maya: go ahead and evict the safe ones. I'm going to flip fallback routing now.

deploy-bot: scheduled action queued: `route-fallback enable --region us-east-1 --variant=cpu-quantized --weight=0.25` will start rolling in 15s.

eng-oncall-maya: executed fallback routing enable. Traffic now split 75/25 to primary GPU model -> CPU-quantized variant. p95 immediately dropped to ~1.2s for the fallback path, overall p95 down to 1.1s, p99 still elevated. Backlog growth rate reduced but not yet reversed.

sre-jamie: I see autoscaler still failing to create new GPU instances due to rate limit. Initiating internal override: `infra-ops-raj` can you trigger our emergency cloud request? Provide request id to cloud support.

infra-ops-raj: opened support case CS-20260315-4498 with provider, asked for immediate instance create allowance for us-east-1 for next 60m. Also initiated eviction of 12 idle GPUs from batch-pool-a. Those nodes will be available in ~90s.

incident-bot: :bookmark_tabs: ACTIONS LOGGED: fallback routing enabled, 12 idle GPUs evicted, cloud support case opened CS-20260315-4498.

eng-oncall-maya: rerouting complete. starting to drain queue consumers onto freed GPUs. running: `rbctl pool scale --name gpu-prod --add 12 --region us-east-1` — hitting api errors until freed allocations appear.

sre-jamie: pool manager now shows 12 nodes provisioned from evicted batch pool. autoscaler create errors dropping. queue length peaked at 126k, now 118k and decreasing slowly. p99 still high at 18s, but that's improvement. Need to monitor for 30m and then rollback fallback.

pm-lee: preparing a short status page update: "We've experienced a traffic surge affecting hosted-api in us-east-1 causing elevated request latency and timeouts. We've enabled fallback routing and reclaimed capacity; service recovery in progress. No data loss. We'll post updates every 15 minutes." Carla to post once approved.

carla-cust-success: posted status update to status.redwood.ai/incidents/1763142593 and DM'd top 5 enterprise account owners. Getting replies, some heavy traffic customers requesting rate-limits. I'll coordinate next steps.

eng-night-oncall-kai: taking point for monitoring through the night. Handoff: eng-oncall-maya, anything left undone before I take over? :wave:

eng-oncall-maya: handoff: watch queue length and autoscaler errors, keep fallback at 25% until p99 < 5s for 10m, if backlog < 40k start rolling fallback down by 10% every 5m. escalation path: if autoscaler errors return, call infra-ops-raj and open incident bridge.

infra-ops-raj: cloud provider approved temporary quota increase (CS-20260315-4498 resolved, +20 GPUs for 60m). Leaving the 12 evicted GPUs allocated. I'll keep noncritical batch jobs bumped out for 60m.

sre-jamie: postmortem notes to capture: shard hard cap + unexpected traffic routing pattern (spike concentrated on one shard) + autoscaler create rate limits. Mitigations: add cross-shard overflow routing, pre-warm capacity for known big customers, change autoscaler retry/backoff and implement fast path to reclaim batch GPUs automatically.

eng-oncall-maya: marking incident status: Mitigated -> partial service restored. Will convert to P1 incident document and hand to SRE for root-cause and long-term fixes. Thanks team. :tada:

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated, on-call handoff to eng-night-oncall-kai. Timeline and actions recorded. Next update in 15m or on change.

eng-night-oncall-kai: ack. monitoring. will post if any regressions.
